data.title: Chinese Shares Lifted as Beijing Signals More Market Support
data.description:
By Sherry Qin

Chinese stocks were lifted as authorities reiterated support for capital markets and vowed stabilization policies, amid increased volatility in global markets.

According to state media Xinhua News Agency, Chinese Premier Li Qiang on Friday chaired a State Council executive meeting focused on market reforms.

The meeting noted that "the capital market is crucial to the overall economic development," and China would improve its market stabilization mechanism and introduce new policies to promote stable and healthy markets, Xinhua reported.

As part of this, the role of China's state investors--the so-called "national team"--in stabilizing the markets and countering volatility would be strengthened. Also, efforts would be made to optimize the function of Central Huijin, a unit of state-owned sovereign wealth fund China Investment, as a quasi-stabilization fund.

It also said that Beijing will guide medium- and long-term funds into the markets and listed companies should be encouraged to pay more dividends and step up share repurchases.

Although the measures look to be mostly reiterating previously announced ones, the language has shifted incrementally to show a bit more urgency and tangible action, according to ING chief China economist Lynn Song.

Chinese stock markets have weakened in recent months, broadly in line with global market as investors cool on tech-related companies. The U.S.'s recent efforts to tighten AI chips exports and renewed tariffs have also weighed on investor sentiment.

The benchmark Shanghai Composite Index has fallen over 15% from its peak in May but picked up on Friday, likely supported by the signals of support from Beijing.

The Shanghai Composite Index was recently up 3.6%, the Shenzhen Composite Index was 6.8% higher and the tech-heavy ChiNext Price Index surged 10.6%, on track for its biggest one-day percentage gain in over two years.

Rule 8 – Dealing Disclosure Requirements

Under Rule 8.3(b) of the Irish Takeover Rules, any person ‘interested’ (directly or indirectly) in 1% or more of any class of ‘relevant securities’ of DCC Energy must disclose all ‘dealings’ in such ‘relevant securities’ during the ‘offer period’. This requirement will continue until the ‘offer period’ ends. If two or more persons co-operate on the basis of any agreement either express or tacit, either oral or written, to acquire an ‘interest’ in ‘relevant securities’ of DCC Energy, they will be deemed to be a single person for the purpose of Rule 8.3 of the Irish Takeover Rules. A dealing disclosure must contain the details specified in Rule 8.6(b) of the Irish Takeover Rules, including details of the dealing concerned and of the person’s interests and short positions in any ‘relevant securities’ of DCC Energy.

All ‘dealings’ in ‘relevant securities’ of DCC Energy by Bidco, or by any party ‘acting in concert’ with Bidco, must also be disclosed by no later than 12:00 noon (London time) on the ‘business day’ following the date of the relevant transaction. If two or more persons co-operate on the basis of an agreement, either express or tacit, either oral or written, to acquire for one or more of them an interest in relevant securities, they will be deemed to be a single person for these purposes.

Disclosure tables, giving details of the companies in whose ‘relevant securities’ and ‘dealings’ should be disclosed, can be found on the Irish Takeover Panel’s website at www.irishtakeoverpanel.ie.

‘Interests’ in securities arise, in summary, when a person has long economic exposure, whether conditional or absolute, to changes in the price of securities. In particular, a person will be treated as having an ‘interest’ by virtue of the ownership or control of securities, or by virtue of any option in respect of, or derivative referenced to, securities.

data.description:

CBOT March wheat is biased to retest a resistance at $5.91-1/4 per bushel, a break above which could lead to a gain into $5.94-1/4 to $5.97 range.

The market looks neutral in a narrow range of $5.81-1/2 to $5.89-1/2. However, the bias is toward the upside, as the bounce triggered by the support at $5.78-1/2 may consist of three waves.

So far, only two have unfolded. The third wave, the wave c is expected to travel into $5.94-1/4 to $5.97 range. A break below $5.81-1/2 may cause a fall into $5.73-3/4 to $5.76-1/2 range.

On the daily chart, the contract is riding on a wave C, which has travelled below its 100% projection level. It is likely to extend to $5.48-1/2, the 138.2% level.

The doji during the previous session and the bullish divergence on the hourly RSI suggest that the market may bounce first before resuming its fall.

data.title: Shearwater announces third quarter 2026 results
data.description:
Bergen, 27 November 2026 – Shearwater Geoservices AS (“Shearwater” or the “Company”) today published the third quarter 2026 results. Revenue in the quarter was USD 107.0 million compared to USD 146.5 million in the third quarter of 2025. EBITDA was USD 14.7 million, (USD 5.2 million) reflecting a continued slow marine contract acquisition market in line with expectations.

Key takeaways:

· Soft Q3 contract activity due to few awards through 1H 2026

· Continued strong multi-client revenue contribution of USD 36 million

· 59% fleet utilisation across 7.3 active vessels, including one OBN crew

· End-Q3 backlog up 3.5x from Q2 to USD 755 million driven by strategic client awards

· Materially improved 2027 visibility, with three vessels fully committed for the year and high H1 coverage

Irene Basili, CEO of Shearwater, comments on the third quarter results:

"The third quarter reflected a continued soft contract market as anticipated, with low fleet utilisation following few projects awarded through first half of the year. At the same time, we benefitted from the organic build-up of our multi-client business with another strong quarterly contribution. We also made material commercial progress with several contract awards and new industry-backed multi-client surveys. We ended the quarter with a record USD 755 million backlog and a strong foundation for increased activity in the fourth quarter and into 2027.

Although it is too early to conclude that a sustained market recovery is underway, our visibility into 2027 is substantially improved. We have three vessels fully committed throughout the year and strong coverage across the active fleet for the first half. Additionally, more than 50% of our backlog comprises multi-year programmes, extending our scheduling horizon. The two large India surveys and the three-year OBN award offshore South America are important contributors, with the latter demonstrating the commercial potential of SW Tasman/Pearl platform.

That said, I want to emphasise that the stronger backlog does not change our commitment to disciplined fleet deployment and cost control. We prioritise utilisation for our active fleet at improved margins and are not planning for any vessel reactivations.

Our multi-client business reached two milestones in the period. First, we have commenced the Amapá survey offshore Brazil with SLB, a major programme adjacent to the Morpho discovery. Secondly, we just completed our first stand-alone survey in the Norwegian Sea. Both projects deploy our state-of-the-art Isometrix technology.

Recent awards, improved forward coverage and ongoing customer discussions are encouraging, and reflect the need for reserve replacement, energy security and exploration. Our focus remains on efficient operational delivery, securing quality backlog and investing selectively in multi-client opportunities. We enter the coming year with materially improved visibility and a more favourable market backdrop, while maintaining discipline on capacity and investments."

data.title: REG - Coca-Cola HBC AG - Completion of CCBA acquisition
data.description:
RNS Number : 9779E Coca-Cola HBC AG 27 November 2026  

FOR IMMEDIATE RELEASE.

Coca-Cola HBC AG

Completion of CCBA acquisition

Zug, Switzerland, 27 November 2026. Coca-Cola HBC AG ("Coca-Cola HBC" or the "Company") is pleased to announce the completion of the Acquisition1 of Coca-Cola Beverages Africa ("CCBA") ("Completion"). Further to its announcement on 16 November 2026, Coca-Cola HBC is also pleased to confirm that it has received merger control approval from the Fair Competition Commission of Tanzania.

The Acquisition brings together two leading Coca-Cola bottlers, and Coca-Cola HBC is now the second-largest Coca-Cola bottler globally by volume[2], serving approximately 1.2 billion consumers and employing nearly 50,000 people.

Building on Coca-Cola HBC’s origins in Nigeria 75 years ago and its expansion into Egypt in 2022, the Acquisition materially expands Coca-Cola HBC’s presence in Africa, adding 14 markets and creating a stronger platform for sustainable, profitable growth. Coca-Cola HBC will now represent approximately two-thirds of Africa's Coca-Cola system volume and serve more than half of the continent's population, strengthening Coca-Cola HBC's position in a highly attractive growth region.

The transaction combines Coca-Cola HBC’s scale, resources and capabilities with CCBA’s strong market positions and deep local knowledge. It supports Coca-Cola HBC’s ambition to be the leading 24/7 beverage partner and it reinforces its long-standing strategic partnership with The Coca-Cola Company.

Anastassis G. David, Chairman of the Board of Coca-Cola HBC, commented:

“Today marks an important new chapter for us in Africa. As we welcome CCBA into the Coca-Cola HBC family, we do so with great respect for the legacy that has been built over generations and with a commitment to strengthening it for the future.

“On behalf of the Board, I would like to thank all the teams involved for their support in bringing this transaction to completion.”

Zoran Bogdanovic, Chief Executive Officer of Coca-Cola HBC, commented:

“The completion of the CCBA acquisition marks a historic milestone for Coca-Cola HBC. Africa is where our business began 75 years ago, and this acquisition significantly strengthens our presence across this incredible continent, creating a strong platform for sustainable, profitable growth. Our listing on the Johannesburg Stock Exchange this week further underlines our long-term commitment to South Africa and the broader African continent.

"CCBA is a high-quality business with strong market positions, deep local knowledge and talented people. We are very pleased to welcome our new colleagues to Coca-Cola HBC. Together, we will invest in our leading 24/7 portfolio, our bespoke capabilities and our passionate people to capture the significant opportunities ahead.

“Our integration planning has been underway for many months, and we are ready to begin the next chapter of our growth story together with confidence and ambition.

"I would like to thank The Coca-Cola Company and the Gutsche family for their trust and partnership, and our teams across CCBA, Coca-Cola HBC and the wider Coca-Cola system for their commitment in completing this transaction. We look forward to working together to drive joint success."

Henrique Braun, Chief Executive Officer of The Coca-Cola Company, commented:

“This transaction reflects the strength of the Coca-Cola system and our long-term commitment to building locally led, world-class bottling operations.

“CCBA has established a strong foundation across Africa, and Coca-Cola HBC brings proven capabilities, deep market expertise and a successful track record of investing for sustainable growth.”

Structure and financial effects

Coca-Cola HBC has acquired a 75% shareholding in CCBA from The Coca-Cola Company (TCCC) and Gutsche Family Investments Pty Ltd (GFI), for a combined purchase price of $2.6 billion (at the time of signing). Coca-Cola HBC and TCCC have entered into a separate option agreement providing Coca-Cola HBC the opportunity to acquire, or TCCC to sell, the remaining 25% stake in CCBA held by TCCC within a six-year period, with the call option exercisable between three and five years following Completion.

In connection with the Acquisition, Coca-Cola HBC will today issue 21,027,676 new ordinary shares to GFI, representing 5.45% of Coca-Cola HBC's enlarged issued and outstanding share capital. Admission to trading of the new ordinary shares on the Main Market of the London Stock Exchange, the Main Board of the Johannesburg Stock Exchange and the Main Market of Euronext Athens is expected to occur on Monday, 30 November 2026 at 08:00 (GMT), 09:00 (SAST) and 10:15 (EET), respectively.

The cash consideration for the Acquisition has been funded through a combination of existing liquidity and bonds issued by Coca-Cola HBC in March 2026 to refinance the bridge facilities entered into at signing. Leverage is expected to remain within Coca-Cola HBC’s medium-term target range of 1.5-2.0x Net debt to EBITDA. Coca-Cola HBC reconfirms that the transaction is expected to be low-single digit EPS accretive from the first full financial year post Completion.

For the purposes of UKLR 7.3.3R, Coca-Cola HBC confirms that there has been no material change affecting any matter contained in the announcement of the Acquisition.

data.title: Indian firms utilising only 20%-30% of free trade agreement benefits, RBI governor says
data.description:
By Ashwin Manikandan

Indian businesses are using only about 20%-30% of the benefits available under free-trade agreements (FTAs) compared with their foreign counterparts, Reserve Bank of India Governor Sanjay Malhotra said at an event in Mumbai on Friday.

  • The comments come days after Prime Minister Narendra Modi said ⁠Indian industry should take advantage of opportunities from the free-trade agreements India has signed, including those with the ​EU and the ​UK

  • "The government of India has now opened up a number of avenues. A number of FTAs have been signed. At the same time, however, it has been found that only about 20% to 30% of the utilization has been done by Indians vis-à-vis 60% to 70% by our partners in the trade agreements," Malhotra said at an event for small and medium businesses

  • There is a long way to go for Indian businesses to take advantage of the lower tariffs negotiated under the agreements, he said

  • Small and medium businesses should learn more about the FTAs to improve quality, delivery timelines, standards and certifications, Malhotra added

  • The micro, small and medium enterprises sector has an AI adoption rate of about 14%, behind peers such as China, Malhotra said

  • India has free-trade agreements with the UK, Oman and New Zealand. Its proposed free-trade agreement with the European Union is expected to accelerate market-access ​opportunities and ​investment ⁠flows between India and the ⁠27-member ​EU bloc

  • Separately, ‌India's Trade Minister Piyush Goyal said on Friday that India and the US were close ​to wrapping up a long-anticipated trade deal

  • Modi told industry leaders last week that Indian businesses could not take their huge domestic market for granted and urged them to compete globally ‌in an era when resources were being weaponised

data.title: As France's problems multiply, so do its presidential hopefuls
data.description:
Key points:
  • Judo champion, ex-PM, Riviera mayor shake up France's 2027 race
  • Proliferation of candidates highlights decline of traditional party machines
  • Le Pen, Melenchon remain clear frontrunners despite crowded field

By Michel Rose

A judo champion, a Riviera mayor and a former French prime minister are the latest pretenders to the Elysee, but despite injecting some intrigue into the presidential election none of them have dislodged far-right leader Marine Le Pen and hard-left veteran Jean-Luc Melenchon from the top of the polls.

In the past few weeks five-time Olympic judo champion Teddy Riner declared his intention to run, former Prime Minister Dominique de Villepin launched a long-anticipated campaign, and David Lisnard, the mayor of Cannes, has surged in opinion polls, overtaking former Prime Minister Edouard Philippe in some surveys.

President Emmanuel Macron's insurgent victory nearly a decade ago shattered the traditional party system, but his rise has hollowed out the political centre and encouraged a growing cast of hopefuls. There are more than 30 declared or prospective candidates.

"Governing parties have weakened and candidates increasingly emerge from the media spotlight," Socialist lawmaker Romain Eskenazi told Reuters. "People say: 'Why not me?'"

For now, polls suggest the crowded field may be helping rather than hurting the two frontrunners by leaving them without a credible mainstream rival who can marshal support from moderate, centre-right and mainstream-left voters.

With France rocked by protests and politicians struggling to tame a bulging deficit, many voters appear unimpressed by the presidential offering.

In a November 12 Odoxa poll for Le Figaro, more than three-quarters of respondents said the high number of candidates showed that "many people have overinflated egos".

RIGHTWINGER LISNARD SURGES, OTHERS WAIT IN WINGS

Lisnard is the best performer so far after Le Pen and Melenchon. The free-market conservative scored 11% in a recent RTL-Toluna poll, ahead of Philippe on 9%, pushing Macron's former prime minister into fifth place behind centre-left candidate Raphael Glucksmann.

Lisnard argues that France's establishment has failed to tackle debt, crime and red tape. He has echoed Argentine President Javier Milei by filming himself shredding regulations.

Long regarded as the strongest contender from France's pro-business centre, Philippe has been the main loser from Lisnard's rise, with some saying his campaign lacks momentum and clear ideas.

But others dismiss Lisnard's rise as temporary.

"I think it's a bubble," Pieyre-Alexandre Anglade, a lawmaker from Macron's party, told Reuters.

At the annual mayors' gathering in Paris, where candidates seek endorsements to make the ballot, many officials remained undecided. Eric Berlivet, mayor of Roche-la-Moliere near Lyon, said he admired both Lisnard and Philippe, and would pick his candidate in January.

"We've been disappointed too often by national leaders," he said. "I want someone who makes everyday life easier."

There has been talk of a primary between the centrist and rightwing candidates, but the politicians have so far not agreed on a process.

"Marine Le Pen and Jean-Luc Melenchon may be leading the polls, but our responsibility is to unite the centre and the right, not launch a primary that would sow confusion and deepen divisions," Jeremie Patrier-Leitus, a spokesperson for Philippe's campaign, told Reuters.

Despite having no political experience, Riner polls around 4%, outperforming several established party leaders such as Greens leader Marine Tondelier and Communist veteran Fabien Roussel. De Villepin, who has won support for his pro-Palestinian views, polls around 3%.

Riner presents himself as an outsider with fresh ideas. Asked at the mayors' conference whether he was entering the race because politicians were not up to the job, he said: "I wouldn't have necessarily phrased it like that, but yes."

There has also been speculation about a possible late run by European Central Bank chief Christine Lagarde, who will step down in February — two months before the April first-round vote. She scored as much as 14% in a recent poll for Politico, but she has remained mum about her intentions.

Former Socialist President Francois Hollande has said he is also mulling putting his name forward.

LE PEN AND MELENCHON UNAFFECTED SO FAR

Christian Le Bart, a political scientist at Sciences Po Rennes, said, "Being outside the main political parties has become an asset."

But it also has its limits.

Riner has appeared to struggle on some policy questions and challenged mainstream thinking by saying "Ukraine was not our war". Meanwhile, de Villepin's failed 2012 presidential campaign showed how hard it can be to secure the 500 signatures from elected officials needed to make the ballot.

While the centre and traditional parties of left and right splinter into competing candidacies, Le Pen and Melenchon continue to dominate. Le Pen remains the candidate to beat, leading most first-round polls and runoff scenarios. A Paris appeals court in July upheld an embezzlement conviction for Le Pen but set the terms of her ban from public office in a way that still allows her to run, though she has appealed to the Court of Cassation, France's highest court.

"She is seen as winning in almost all the second-round scenarios," Le Bart said, adding that her decade-long normalisation strategy had changed her National Rally party's image.

However, he warned against concluding it was a done deal, as the field will inevitably narrow as the vote nears, injecting unpredictability.

"The race is far from over," he said.

data.title: HDFC Bank shares tread water as rally loses steam
data.description:
HDFC Bank shares were nearly flat on Friday, edging up just 0.10 per cent to ₹862.85 on the NSE, as the week's strong momentum faded and volumes dropped sharply, pointing to a consolidation phase after a near-30 per cent rebound from October lows.

The stock opened at ₹857.90, touched a high of ₹866.25, and saw no fresh leg higher. Traded value fell to ₹1,472.53 crore on volume of 170.76 lakh shares, roughly half Thursday's traded value, with sellers accounting for 68 per cent of total traded quantity. Delivery-based trades stood at 69 per cent, suggesting the remaining activity was largely short-term in nature.

There were no exchange filings from the bank on Friday. This week's key corporate development was Wednesday's board approval of Dr Harsh Kumar Bhanwala's re-appointment as Independent Director for a fresh five-year term from January 2027, subject to shareholder approval.

The NSE flagged that HDFC Bank's close-to-close price movement exceeded 25 per cent in the prior month, a standard surveillance indicator triggered by the stock's sharp recovery from its 52-week low of ₹669.20 on October 28.

HDFC Bank's year-to-date loss stood at 13.01 per cent, against the Nifty 50's 1.68 per cent decline. The stock trades at a P/E of 16.61 and remains roughly 15 per cent below its 52-week high of ₹1,017.50.

Bank Nifty consolidated near 63,535, with analysts watching the 64,000 mark as the next decisive trigger.

data.title: REG - Tooru PLC - New funding facility and related party transaction
data.description:
RNS Number : 8907E Tooru PLC 27 November 2026  

27 November 2026

Tooru plc

(“Tooru” or the “Company”)

New funding facility and related party transaction

Tooru, the AIM listed company focused on the branded health and wellness sector, is pleased to announce that it has entered into a funding facility (the “Facility”) with S-Ventures plc (“SVEN”) to provide the Company with additional funding for continued investment into the Company’s principal operating businesses and for the Company’s ’s working capital requirements.

The Facility

The Facility is a two-year unsecured facility for up to £500,000 and is expected to be drawn down in tranches of £100,000.  Each drawdown will require approval of the Board of SVEN and will be subject to prevailing market conditions at the time of any drawdown request.  Annual interest of 5% will accrue on each drawdown and principal and interest for each drawdown will be repayable on the second anniversary of each drawdown date.

Additionally, on each drawdown, Tooru will issue to SVEN two separate tranches of warrants over the Company’s ordinary shares. The number of warrants to be issued in the first tranche (the “First Tranche Warrants”) will be calculated by dividing the amount drawn down (the “Drawdown Amount”) by the Company’s closing share price on the trading day immediately prior to the issue of a drawdown notice (the “Reference Price”) and multiplied by 1.5. The First Tranche Warrants will have an exercise price equal to the Reference Price. The number of warrants to be issued in the second tranche of warrants (the “Second Tranche Warrants” and together with the First Tranche Warrants, the “Warrants”) will be calculated by dividing the Drawdown Amount by the Reference Price increased by a premium of 78 per cent. (the "Second Tranche Exercise Price"). The exercise price of the Second Tranche Warrants will be equal to the Second Tranche Exercise Price. The life of both Warrants will be 3 years from their date of issue.

Related party transaction

By virtue of its significant shareholding of 14.91% in the Company and commonality of a director, Scott Livingston, SVEN is a related party as defined in the AIM Rules.  Accordingly, the entering into the Facility is considered to be a Related Party Transaction ("Transaction") pursuant to Rule 13 of the AIM Rules. Mr Livingston has been recused from the formal consideration of the Transaction by the Board.

The Directors of the Company who are independent of the Transaction, having consulted with the Company's Nominated Adviser, Beaumont Cornish, consider the terms of the Transaction to be fair and reasonable insofar as the Company's shareholders are concerned.

Scott Livingston, CEO of Tooru plc, commented:

“The Company continues to demonstrate strong momentum in building its various businesses.  This funding facility will provide additional funds for further investment into the Company’s key businesses and for general working capital purposes.”

data.title: REG - M. P. Evans Group - Crop & production update; share buyback programme
data.description:
RNS Number : 8841E M. P. Evans Group PLC 27 November 2026  

M.P. EVANS GROUP PLC

(“M.P. Evans”, “the Group”, or “the Company”)

STRONG CROP AND PRODUCTION GROWTH AND FURTHER £2 MILLION SHARE BUYBACK ALLOCATION

M.P. Evans Group PLC, a producer of sustainable Indonesian palm oil, is pleased to announce continued strong crop and production growth during the second half of 2026, and that the Group is allocating a further £2 million to its existing share-buyback programme.

In the 2026 interim results announcement on 14 September 2026, the Group reported that the total crop harvested during the first half of the year from the areas managed by it (including own hectarage plus that managed on behalf of associated scheme smallholders) was 705,400 tonnes, up by 14% from the same period in the previous year. This strong performance has continued through to the end of October with the equivalent figure for the ten-month year-to-date increase remaining at 14%. Despite an extended period of dry weather in several of the Group’s properties in the middle part of the year, Group estates have performed well, and the board anticipates that recent rainfall will continue to support cropping levels during the last quarter.

Again, consistent with the position at the half-year, total crop processed for the ten months to October 2026 is up by 8% as the Group continues to restrict the amount of lower margin outside crop brought in for processing. However, pleasingly, total crude palm oil (“CPO”) output is now up by 13% on the same point last year, as oil-extraction rates have continued to improve during the second half of the year. This increase in production has also helped to further reduce unit costs from the amounts reported in the interim results. The Group is working hard to ensure that production is despatched on a timely basis, but there may be a small amount of carryover into 2027 which will be of benefit to that year’s results.

Pricing for the Group’s output has, thus far, remained at similar levels in the second half of 2026 with the year-to-date ex-mill-gate price for the Group’s CPO at US$866 per tonne for the ten months to October, only 1% different to the US$873 reported at June. There may be some slight price softening towards the end of the year, with supply increasing and good stocks available, notably in Malaysia, but we anticipate some price recovery in early 2027.

Indonesia has experienced the effect of the El Nino weather phenomenon during 2026, and this may lead to a small reduction in total national palm oil output in 2027. By contrast, production from Group estates is expected to remain robust, benefiting from a combination of geographic diversity, natural yield increases as several young areas continue to mature, and management’s continuing commitment to high agronomic standards across the Group’s estate portfolio.

The Group announced on 5 October 2026 that it was extending its share buyback programme with a budget of £3 million, and set out in that announcement the basis upon which the programme was being implemented. Given the ongoing strength of the Group’s performance, the board has decided to allocate a further £2 million to the programme (on the same basis as disclosed in the 5 October 2026 announcement) with immediate effect.

The Group will provide a further trading update for the whole of 2026 in its crop, pricing and production announcement due to be released in January 2027.

M.P. Evans Group PLC chief executive Matthew Coulson commented on the Group’s performance:

“As we move into the closing stages of 2026, the Group has continued to perform well, both operationally and financially, and the board is confident that the Group will deliver some excellent results for the year as a whole.”

data.title: REG - Jadestone Energy PLC - Publication of Circular and Notice of Meeting
data.description:
RNS Number : 9773E Jadestone Energy PLC 27 November 2026  

Publication of Circular and Notice of Requisitioned General Meeting

Board unanimously recommends that shareholders vote AGAINST all the Resolutions to stop Prima Energy gaining control of Jadestone without paying a control premium

27 November 2026 – Singapore: Jadestone Energy plc (AIM:JSE) (the “Company” and together with its subsidiaries, “Jadestone”), an independent upstream production and development company focused on the Asia-Pacific region, announces that, following the requisition notice received on 20 November 2026 on behalf of PT Prima Petroleum Energi (“Prima Energy”), it has today published a circular to shareholders (the “Circular”) containing notice of a general meeting of the Company (the “Requisitioned General Meeting”) to be held at 1.00 p.m. (GMT) on Monday, 21 December 2026 at the offices of K&L Gates LLP, 5th Floor, One New Change, London EC4M 9AF.

At the Requisitioned General Meeting, shareholders will be asked to consider two ordinary resolutions, proposed by Prima Energy, to appoint Pieters Adyana Utomo, Chief Executive Officer of Prima Energy and Alexander Paul Blakeley OBE, former President and CEO of Jadestone Energy, as directors of the Company (the “Resolutions”). The Circular also contains a statement by Prima Energy, which the Company is required to circulate under section 314 of the Companies Act 2006.

The Circular, which includes the Notice of Requisitioned General Meeting, has been published on the Company’s website at www.jadestone-energy.com and is being posted to shareholders today, together with a Form of Proxy.

JADESTONE’S BOARD OF DIRECTORS UNANIMOUSLY RECOMMENDS THAT SHAREHOLDERS VOTE AGAINST ALL THE PRIMA ENERGY RESOLUTIONS.

Dr. Adel Chaouch, Executive Chairman of Jadestone Energy, commented:

“The fiduciary duty of Jadestone’s Board of Directors is to protect and create value for all shareholders.  Prima Energy is clearly a competitor of Jadestone and, in the Board’s view, is displaying a clear intent to opportunistically take control of the Company. The Board urges shareholders to vote and unanimously recommends that shareholders vote AGAINST all the Resolutions to stop Prima Energy from taking control of your company without paying an appropriate premium for all shareholders and using proprietary information for its own purposes to the detriment of shareholders.”

It is clear to the Board that Prima Energy’s ultimate goal is to gain control of the Company without paying an appropriate premium to its shareholders. The Board considers that Prima Energy’s arguments in support of the Resolutions are self-serving and an attempt to secure Board representation and access to proprietary information without an appropriate relationship agreement in place that protects the rights of all shareholders. The Board believes that this would be detrimental to all other Jadestone shareholders and potentially lead to a destruction of shareholder value.

The Board set out the background to the requisition in its announcement of 23 November 2026. The letter from the Chairman in the Circular sets out the Board’s full reasons for its recommendation, including the following:

  • On 2 September 2026, Prima Energy announced that it had agreed to acquire approximately 28.3 per cent. of the Company’s issued share capital from funds managed by Tyrus Capital S.A.M. (“Tyrus Capital”) and stated that it had no intention of making an offer for the Company, a statement by which it is bound under Rule 2.8 of the Takeover Code. The Board understands that Prima Energy paid a very substantial premium to the average share price over the month prior to the acquisition, with Prima Energy repeatedly refusing to disclose the price it paid.
  • On 7 September 2026, Prima Energy proposed to the Company what was effectively a deed of control. Among other things, it:
    • would have entitled Prima Energy to nominate two directors while holding 20 per cent. or more, whom the Company would have been obliged to appoint without any assessment by the Board or its Nominated Adviser;
    • would have entitled Prima Energy to place each of its directors on every Board committee; and to receive, each quarter, monthly production by field, operating cost per barrel, realised prices and capital expenditure; and
    • contained no standstill, which is a key protection for other shareholders against Prima Energy having a route to control without paying shareholders a premium for it.
  • Although the draft deed of control was subsequently withdrawn, the Board believes that Prima Energy’s underlying aim remains unchanged.
  • At the same time as proposing the deed of control, Prima Energy proposed that the Company's Chairman should step down from the Board, with Mr Utomo and Mr Blakeley to join the Board, as part of Prima Energy's proposed “leadership transition”.
  • On 28 October 2026, the Company offered Prima Energy the right to nominate one director, subject to a relationship agreement based on the agreement formerly in place with Tyrus Capital, with the addition of further protections reflecting Prima Energy’s position as a direct competitor and the manner of acquisition of its shares (no price having been disclosed) and the previous interactions on the deed of control. Prima Energy rejected this offer. Since 28 October 2026, designated members of the Board have had various interactions with Mr Utomo and Prima Energy on the content of an appropriate relationship agreement.
  • Prima Energy is a direct competitor of the Company in its core operating areas and has refused to enter into a relationship agreement that the Board considers would protect the rights of all shareholders. Prima Energy has also repeatedly asked to appoint a director to the Board with no relationship agreement in place at all, which the Board considers a disregard for basic governance norms and evidence of a desire to access Company information without restraint. Neither of the proposed directors can be considered independent. Mr Utomo is also President Director of PT Soechi Lines Tbk, a vessel owner and operator, and the Company’s potential service providers may be reluctant to bid for its contracts if the head of a competing service provider sits on its Board.
  • The Board does not consider that the return of Mr Blakeley, a former executive of the Company and the nominee of a single shareholder, is consistent with the Company’s governance framework or the orderly leadership transition completed under the current Board. In early November 2026, Prima Energy met several of the Company’s shareholders in the UK. Although Mr Utomo had advised the Company that Prima Energy would not take the discussions about two Board seats to shareholders and that he had “disengaged” from Mr Blakeley, Mr Blakeley represented Prima Energy at all of those meetings, with Board composition, including the intention to seek two Board seats, a central topic.
  • The Board does not consider Prima Energy’s request comparable to the Board representation previously granted to significant shareholders. Tyrus Capital and Livermore Partners were effectively founder shareholders, were not competitors of the Company and provided early-stage capital to build the Company. Prima Energy is a new shareholder and a competitor seeking control without paying a control premium to shareholders.
  • The Company continues to target a final investment decision on its Vietnam gas development before the end of 2026. The Requisitioned General Meeting diverts the Company’s time and resources from that Vietnam gas development at a critical point.
  • The Board has consulted the Company’s largest institutional shareholders. There was a clear consensus that no Board seat should be provided to Prima Energy without an appropriate relationship agreement. Of the shareholders consulted, no shareholder supported two Board seats for Prima Energy, and some opposed even a single seat.

If Prima Energy wants control of the Company, it should make an offer to all shareholders at a price that reflects the value of control.

Action to be taken

Shareholders are encouraged to vote AGAINST all the Resolutions, whether or not they intend to attend the meeting. Proxy appointments, whether made by Form of Proxy, online, through CREST or through Proxymity, must be received by the Company’s Registrar, Computershare Investor Services PLC, by 1.00 p.m. (GMT) on Thursday, 17 December 2026. Shareholders who hold their shares through an investment platform or other nominee should note that the platform’s deadline may be earlier. Shareholders with questions about the Requisitioned General Meeting or how to vote may contact Georgeson at jse@georgeson.com.

About Jadestone

Jadestone Energy plc is an independent upstream company focused on the Asia-Pacific region. It has a balanced and increasingly diversified portfolio of production and development assets in Australia, Malaysia, Indonesia and Vietnam, all stable jurisdictions with a positive upstream investment climate.

The Company is pursuing a strategy to grow and diversify the Company’s production base both organically, through developments such as Nam Du/U Minh in Vietnam and the Puteri Cluster offshore Malaysia, as well as through acquisitions that fit within Jadestone’s financial framework and play to the Company’s strengths in regional upstream development and operations and managing maturing oil assets. Jadestone delivers value in its acquisition strategy by enhancing returns through operating efficiencies, cost reductions and increased production through further investment.

Jadestone is a responsible operator and well positioned for the energy transition through its increasing gas production, by maximising recovery from existing brownfield developments and through its Net Zero pledge on Scope 1 & 2 GHG emissions from operated assets by 2040. This strategy is aligned with the IEA Net Zero by 2050 scenario, which stresses the necessity of continued investment in existing upstream assets to avoid an energy crisis and meet demand for oil and gas through the energy transition.

Jadestone Energy plc (LEI: 21380076GWJ8XDYKVQ37) is listed on the AIM market of the London Stock Exchange (AIM: JSE). The Company is headquartered in Singapore. For further information on the Company please visit www.jadestone-energy.com.
